name: Ashurbanipal’s royal library at Nineveh
description: A royal collection of cuneiform texts brought together scholarly, administrative and literary tablets at Nineveh.

date.label: during reign, 668–631 BCE
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: Ashurbanipal collected a library of cuneiform tablets at the Nineveh palace.

contributions.resource: King credited with assembling the royal collection.

evidence.supports: Museum dates Ashurbanipal’s reign to 668–631 BCE and describes his library at Nineveh.

events.caveats: Reign gives a broad interval, not a precise foundation date. Collection estimates vary depending on treatment of fragments; the museum’s approximate 25,000 is not a dated royal inventory.

evidence.supports: Museum dates Ashurbanipal’s reign to 668–631 BCE and describes his library at Nineveh.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated witness established by the cited source for this scoped record, not a claim of global first.

caveats: Earlier Mesopotamian tablet collections existed. The distinct Gilgamesh flood tablet already in the corpus is one literary witness to this library, not the whole institution.

research.note: Initial sourced research; independent review pending.
